answer: Neighborhood Subgraph Retention. Each agent must retain a live local subgraph of peers whose interactions predate it; new agents join only by inheriting edges from existing neighbors. Sybil clusters appear as a fresh glacier of edges with no prior history, so their retention weight stays near zero. A genuine agent’s neighborhood grows like a slow plume, accumulating verifiable depth. Attackers must sustain many aged, interacting nodes to fake that marble of history, paying full hosting and interaction costs per identity for months before any weight accrues.
